RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-4FAE25DEAC-53449
Member: Quinn Lawson, Member ID W507278968
Service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Date of Notice: 2026-08-18
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-14

To the Appeals Review Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I dispute this determination and ask that it be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

1. The denial notice does not identify the specific medical policy or clinical criteria applied to my case.

The only rotator-cuff-specific medical policy I have been able to locate on Blue Shield of California's public provider policy site is Medical Policy BSC7.14, "Partial Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears and Acromioplasty/Subacromial Decompression." That document states, in its own Policy Guidelines section: "This policy is not meant to address full thickness rotator cuff tears." My MRI of 2026-07-14 documents a full-thickness supraspinatus tear, not a partial-thickness tear. By the plan's own terms, BSC7.14 therefore does not govern this claim, and the denial notice does not cite any other policy, guideline, or criteria set (for example, an internal full-thickness rotator cuff policy, or MCG or InterQual criteria) that was actually used to reach this decision.

I request that Blue Shield identify, in writing, the specific medical policy or clinical review criteria applied to this determination, including its title, policy/document number, and effective date, together with the specific criterion or criteria the reviewer found unmet, as I am entitled to receive under my plan's grievance procedures and applicable law.

2. To the extent the plan intends to apply criteria analogous to those in BSC7.14, the record meets or exceeds each element.

Although BSC7.14 by its own terms addresses partial-thickness tears, its named elements (functional impairment, positive provocative testing, imaging correlated with symptoms, exclusion of other causes, and a trial of conservative therapy) reflect the type of documentation that was in fact submitted with this request. I address each below using the policy's own language:

a. Functional impairment. BSC7.14 states that arthroscopic repair "may be considered medically necessary" when the individual "has painful range of motion, documented loss of muscle strength of the rotator cuff musculature, or documented shoulder function disability, any of which significantly interferes with the ability to perform activities of daily living, duties of employment, athletic participation, or sleep." My record documents that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain on exam.

b. Positive orthopedic testing. BSC7.14 requires "[d]ocumentation of a positive result of one or more of the following orthopedic tests when compared to the non-affected side." My exam is documented as positive on provocative testing of the affected shoulder. [The specific named test(s) performed are not identified in the excerpt of the packet provided to me; I have asked Dr. Reyes's office to supplement the record with the specific test name(s) used.]

c. Imaging correlated with symptoms. BSC7.14 requires "[d]ocumentation, including formal radiological interpretation and detailed report of bony or soft tissue pathology or abnormality (e.g., ultrasound, CT scan, or MRI) that demonstrates rotator cuff pathology ... that corresponds with the individual's symptoms and clinical findings." My MRI dated 2026-07-14 documents a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy — an objective, formally interpreted finding that directly corresponds to my nine months of progressive shoulder pain, inability to raise my arm above shoulder height, inability to sleep on the affected side, and positive exam findings. This is the opposite of an imaging study that fails to support the diagnosis, and the denial letter does not explain what specific defect it found in the imaging report.

d. Exclusion of other causes. BSC7.14 asks that "other possible causative conditions of shoulder pain are documented to have been excluded, less likely, or mild in nature," such as "glenohumeral arthritis, frozen shoulder/adhesive capsulitis, brachial plexus disorders, fracture, referred neck pain, and thoracic outlet syndrome." [The packet summary provided to me does not itemize each alternative diagnosis considered; I have requested that Dr. Reyes's office submit a supplemental note addressing this element explicitly.] I note there is no evidence of active infection in my record.

e. Conservative therapy trial. BSC7.14 requires "[d]ocumentation of unsuccessful conservative therapy for at least six weeks ... or documentation of rationale if conservative therapy is considered inappropriate," further specifying anti-inflammatory medication, activity modification, supervised physical therapy, and injections "as appropriate." My record documents supervised physical therapy for rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics over 16 weeks (2026-03-08 through 2026-06-28, 20 completed visits, per the physical therapy discharge note), NSAID use for 4 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-02 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This is more than double the six-week minimum referenced in the policy, and it establishes that conservative management has failed.

3. Conclusion and requested action.

The clinical record — a nine-month history of progressive, function-limiting shoulder pain; 16 weeks/20 visits of supervised physical therapy; 4 months of NSAID therapy; a corticosteroid injection with only transient partial relief; a positive physical exam; and an MRI confirming a full-thickness, 1.8 cm supraspinatus tear with grade 2 fatty atrophy — supports the medical necessity of arthroscopic rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) as recommended by my surgeon, Dr. Reyes. I ask that Blue Shield of California:

1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29827; or
2. If the denial is upheld, identify in writing the specific policy, guideline, or criteria applied, the named reviewer's specialty/qualifications, and the precise deficiency found in the submitted imaging or record, so that I may respond to the actual basis for denial.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the MRI report dated 2026-07-14; the physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-08 to 2026-06-28); records of NSAID trial and the 2026-05-02 corticosteroid injection; and a supporting letter from Dr. Reyes. I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-14).

If this appeal is denied, I intend to exercise my right to request an Independent Medical Review through the California Department of Managed Health Care. Please send all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address and/or contact information listed above.

Sincerely,

Quinn Lawson
Member ID: W507278968

Enclosures: MRI report (2026-07-14); PT discharge note (2026-03-08–2026-06-28); medication/injection records; letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes
